title: Housekeeping: roxygen2 8, https URLs, .Rbuildignore
description:
Routine upkeep. Closes #49.

**Set the minimum R version to 4.1, and test it.** `DESCRIPTION` claimed
`R (>= 2.10)`, which has never been true of this package — `paste0()` is used at
13 call sites across 5 files and did not exist until R 2.15.0. Verified against
the actual base sources of R 2.10.1, 2.14.2, 2.15.3 and 3.0.3: absent in 2.14.2,
present in 2.15.3, matching R's own NEWS. 4.1 rather than 2.15.0 because testthat
needs 4.1 to run at all, and because a floor nothing tests is a claim rather than
a guarantee. The matrix previously bottomed out at `oldrel-4` (4.2.3 today), so a
job pinned to `'4.1'` is added — pinned rather than `oldrel-N`, which drifts.

**Regenerate the documentation with roxygen2 8.0.0.** Replaces `RoxygenNote` with
`Config/roxygen2/version`, writes cross-references as `\link[=f]{f()}`, renders
the Posit ROR, and drops trailing whitespace after `Other time:`. No hand-written
documentation changed.

**Use https for the pkgdown site and the cranlogs badge.** `http://` in
`DESCRIPTION`, `_pkgdown.yml`, and the README badge. All three hosts serve https.

**Tidy `.Rbuildignore`.** Drops dead Travis and AppVeyor rules (`.travis.yml` was
listed twice, once escaped and once not; `revdep` also twice) and escapes the dot
in the `README.Rmd` rule.

## Not included

`usethis::use_github_action()` was run for all four workflows and each came back
byte-identical to the current `r-lib/actions@v2` template, so CI templates are
already current.

title: Fix the edge cases in pretty_round() and pretty_signif() from issue 46
description:
Closes #46.

Each item from the audit is its own commit, ordered so that validation lands
before the code that assumes valid input. `devtools::test()` is green after
every commit, not just the last.

| Commit | Issue item |
| --- | --- |
| Return `character(0)` for zero-length input | 3 |
| Check `digits`, `sci_range`, and `sci_sep` | 6 |
| Check the length of `digits` in `pretty_signif()` | 2 |
| Treat `digits` smaller than 1 as 1 | 1 |
| Preserve the `names` and `dim` of `x` | 4 |
| Vectorize the scientific notation mantissa | — (see below) |
| Normalize the scientific notation mantissa | 10 |
| Pad past the digits a double carries with zeros | 9 |
| Document `sci_range` as inclusive at the boundary | 8 |
| Document round-half-even and the sign of a negative zero | 5, and the closing note |

## Decisions worth a second opinion

**`digits < 1` warns and clamps** rather than erroring, matching `signif()`'s
documented "values smaller than 1 are treated as 1". `pretty_round()` is
untouched — negative `digits` is meaningful there.

**Non-integer `digits` is rounded to the nearest integer**, matching base
`round()`. This was internally inconsistent before: `round()` rounded `2.7` to
three decimals while the `formatC()` that followed truncated it to two.

**Item 8 changed the documentation, not the code.** The `>=` behaviour is
already relied on by `pretty_signif(999999, 3, sci_range = 6)`, which rounds up
to `1e6` and is expected to come back as `"1.00e6"`.

**Item 5 is documentation and tests only**, as the issue suggested — `"-0.00"`
matches what `formatC()` does.

## A bug the audit did not list

`pretty_round()` errored outright whenever a scalar `digits` was paired with two
or more values in the scientific range, because `formatC()` does not recycle
`digits`:

```r
pretty_round(c(1e7, 2e7), 3, sci_range = 5)
#> Error in if (digits < 0L) digits <- 6L else { : the condition has length > 1
```

Only single-element scientific output worked, which is why the existing tests
missed it: `pretty_signif()` reaches `pretty_round()` through the
vectorized-`digits` branch, one element per call. `sprintf()` recycles both the
precision and the value.

## On the digit clamp in item 9

The issue suggests clamping at "roughly 15–17". A flat 15 is wrong — it turns

```r
pretty_signif(pi, 16)   #> "3.141592653589790"
```

replacing a real digit with a zero. Instead both renderers emit the fewest
significant digits that reproduce the value exactly and pad the rest with
zeros, so no digit is invented and none is lost. `pretty_signif(pi, 16)` stays
`"3.141592653589793"`, and `pretty_signif(1.234, 30)` is `1.234` followed by
zeros.

One case does not fully clear up: `pretty_signif(1e300, 3, sci_range = Inf)`
still shows noise near the 17th digit, because `round(1e300, -298)` is not
`1e300`. That is upstream of formatting, in base `round()`.
`pretty_round(1e300, 3, sci_range = Inf)`, which does not hit that call, is
exactly `1` followed by 300 zeros and `.000`.

## Verification

- `devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 note, and the note is `.git`
  being visible because I checked from a git worktree.
- An old-versus-new sweep over 76 values spanning `1e-320` to `1e300`
  (positive, negative, zero, denormals, `double.xmax`), `digits` from -9 to 20,
  and `sci_range` in `{0, 3, 5, 6, Inf}` confirms the only behaviour changes are
  the intended ones.
- The `README.Rmd` rounding examples produce unchanged output, so no re-knit.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The one existing snapshot, `pretty_round(1, c(2, 3))`, became an
  `expect_error(..., fixed = TRUE)` on the same message, and
  `tests/testthat/_snaps/rounding.md` is deleted. No new snapshots.
- `man/` was regenerated selectively. The installed roxygen2 is 8.0.0 while the
  package declares `RoxygenNote: 7.2.3`, and a full run also rewrites
  `DESCRIPTION` and four unrelated `.Rd` files. I reverted those to keep the
  diff focused, so a roxygen upkeep pass is still outstanding as separate work.
- No new dependencies — the helpers are base R only, and avoid `strrep()` so
  that `Depends: R(>= 2.10)` stays honest.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to prettyunits website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the prettyunits website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

## Screenshots

title: Remove dependencies
description:
The package is handy for a new package from me, but I try to keep the dependencies minimal. Thus I've removed all remaining dependencies from `prettyunits`:
- `assertthat` was only used for `is.string`. Replaced with `assert_string()` function.
- `methods::is()` was not really required because there already was a helper function `assert_diff_time()` calling `inherits()`.
